title: Ruby wristlet
alt: A low gold-coloured wristlet has narrow loops gathered at the centre.
fact: The museum identifies the small wristlet’s materials as gold and rubies.
focus: Look at the gaps between the loops at the centre.
limit: One-ink proofs cannot carry the ruby colour or distinguish gold from another reflective metal. Keep the material line with the record.

title: Apricot Kashmir shawl
context: Kashmir, Afghan period, according to the museum.
material: 2/2 twill tapestry weave, double interlocked; wool
alt: An apricot shawl has a broad central field and patterned bands at both ends.
fact: The wool shawl has a central field with patterned ends. The museum records 325 × 104.1 cm overall.
focus: Follow the meeting of one end band and the broad field.
limit: The plain field and the end pattern belong to one whole shawl. Keep the overall size with the collection view.

title: Weaving and Spinning
context: The museum credits Kehar Singh. Punjab, probably Amritsar or Lahore.
material: Gum tempera and ink on paper
alt: Small figures use tools in two settings on one sheet of cream paper.
fact: The page painted in gum tempera and ink shows weaving and spinning in two groups. The museum says the words above identify the artist and the workers’ occupations.
focus: Compare the two groups, then look at the upper edge in both pulls. Keep the museum’s reading on its own slip even when dark marks survive.
limit: The museum gives this painting’s place of making as probably Amritsar or Lahore. The words identify what work the people do. Their personal names remain open.

creditSlip.artist: The museum reads Kehar Singh as the artist’s name in the words above the scene.
creditSlip.work: The same inscription also identifies the workers’ occupations. The catalogue gives the work as weaving and spinning.
creditSlip.counter: The runner leaves the first line above the single proof for the queue. The second line rides underneath on the same slip.
creditSlip.drawer: The keeper puts the lines beside the photograph and your two ink tests. Visitors can compare the upper edge and still read both lines on the separate slip.
creditSlip.journal: I pulled two proofs and kept both readings of the inscription on the slip. The museum identifies Kehar Singh and the kinds of work. I could show which marks survived even where I could not read the words from my proof.

title: Sitar with a replacement string
context: Attributed to Bengal or Bangladesh by the museum.
material: Gourd and wood with pigment, ivory, and bone; copper alloy: frets; iron alloy: strings (with one modern copper replacement)
alt: A stringed instrument lies diagonally across the view, with a rounded resonator and a long fretted neck.
fact: The museum records iron alloy strings with one modern copper replacement.
focus: Follow the thin line of the neck away from its round base.
limit: A print of the neck cannot date individual strings or recover this instrument’s earlier sound. Keep the replacement in the condition record.

title: Kandy pepper-flower necklace
context: Attributed to Kandy, in present-day Sri Lanka.
alt: Several thin gold strands hang between two heavier decorated ends.
fact: The museum lists gold and gives the necklace’s name as Siro Bo Maleya, glossed as pepper-flower garland.
focus: Check the gap between two hanging strands.
limit: A bold print can join two adjacent strands. Keep the name with its catalogue entry, which gives no overall measurement.

title: Guan ware brush rest
context: Attributed to Zhejiang, China, Southern Song dynasty.
dimensions: Diameter: 2.8 x 7.6 cm (1 1/8 x 3 in.); Overall: 6 cm (2 3/8 in.)
alt: A low glazed brush rest is shaped as a small range of pale hills.
fact: The museum describes a mountain-shaped glazed stoneware rest with twelve undulating hills.
focus: Follow the outer line where two hills meet.
limit: A single angle can hide one hill behind another. Keep the museum’s description separate from a count made from one proof.

title: Lacquered paper footed tray
material: lacquer over twisted and coiled paper
alt: A low rectangular tray stands on short feet. Its rim is textured.
fact: The museum records twisted and coiled paper beneath the lacquer.
focus: Trace the space below the rim and one foot.
limit: The finished surface leaves the structure of the paper below it hidden in this view. Keep the materials beside the silhouette.

title: Lacquer jar with xingxing
catalogueTitle: Jar with Scenes of Frolicking Xingxing
material: Zelkova wood, covered with hemp cloth and colored lacquer, and bronze-plated wood fittings
dimensions: Diameter: 47.2 cm (18 9/16 in.); Overall: 49.4 cm (19 7/16 in.)
alt: A dark round jar has red bands, small circular motifs and a red animal scene.
fact: The museum dates the jar to 1302 and records a zelkova body covered with hemp cloth and coloured lacquer.
focus: Check where the motif meets the wide dark band.
limit: A one-ink band may lose distinctions between the coloured lacquer and the surrounding dark area. The date belongs to the record for the jar.

title: Half of a Cambodian sampot
alt: A long narrow red textile has a patterned field and narrow bands near its ends.
fact: The museum catalogues a half of a sampot in silk tabby weave with weft ikat.
focus: Follow the narrow edge beside the repeated interior pattern.
limit: The printed outline is for the surviving half. Leave the size and pattern of the missing portion open.

title: Central Javanese cotton slendang
alt: A dark shoulder cloth surrounds a long pale central panel.
fact: The museum records a cotton shoulder cloth in tabby weave with batik decoration.
focus: Look where the narrow central opening meets the patterned cloth.
limit: The opening is a light area of cloth in the museum view. The proof leaves its fibre type to the material record.

title: Northern Javanese silk slendang
context: Attributed to the north coast of Java, Indonesia.
alt: Dense floral shapes run the length of a narrow light cloth.
fact: The museum records a silk shoulder cloth in tabby weave with batik decoration.
focus: Find one patterned repeat near the outer edge.
limit: Batik describes a recorded technique. Similar marks in another impression leave the cloth’s fibre and origin open.

title: Savu selimut
alt: A long dark textile has horizontal patterned registers and a fringe.
fact: The museum identifies the material as ikat-dyed cotton and gives the object type as a selimut.
focus: Check where one grouping of narrow bands ends and the next begins.
limit: A facsimile of the pattern cannot identify an individual person. Keep the attribution and the exact accession on the museum slip.

title: Lampung tampan pasisir
material: tabby weave with supplementary weft; cotton
alt: A red textile shows a large geometric ship form, with patterned bands above and below.
fact: The museum records a ship cloth in cotton tabby weave with supplementary weft.
focus: Follow the outline below the long ship motif.
limit: The woven image preserves a design. The print leaves the construction and journeys of any actual vessel open.

title: Palembang wearing cloth
material: tabby weave; silk brocaded with silk and metallic threads
alt: A reddish woven cloth has repeated small patterns and a central band.
fact: The museum records silk tabby weave brocaded with silk and metallic threads and describes small rosettes in the field.
focus: Compare a rosette in the field with the larger border pattern.
limit: One ink cannot reproduce the surface behaviour of the metallic threads. Keep the original material line.

title: Baekje jar with an impressed surface
catalogueTitle: Jar with Loop Handle with Overall Impressed Surface Decoration
context: Attributed to the Baekje kingdom in Korea.
alt: A rounded earthenware jar has a lightly patterned body. The catalogue image also shows its lid.
fact: This component accession identifies the jar body. The museum records impressed surface decoration.
focus: Look for an impressed mark on the body below the rim.
limit: The lid shown with the jar has a separate component accession. A view of both does not change what this accession identifies.

title: Goryeo box and cover with inlaid design
catalogueTitle: Box and Cover with Inlaid Phoenix Design
dimensions: Diameter: 19.4 cm (7 5/8 in.); Overall: 12.7 cm (5 in.)
alt: A rounded box with a shallow lid has a dense light inlaid pattern.
fact: The museum records an earthenware box and cover with an inlaid phoenix design.
focus: Check the line between the decorated cover and the deeper box.
limit: The view can show a design and a seam. The occasion on which this box was used needs its own source.

title: Goryeo fish-tail spoon
alt: A spoon has an elongated bowl and a slender handle with a split tip.
fact: The museum describes the curved handle as splitting into a jagged fish-tail shape.
focus: See whether the two narrow ends of the handle stay distinct.
limit: A one-ink preview cannot carry the surface finish of silver bronze. The recorded 28.4 cm length belongs to the whole spoon.

title: Goryeo bowl with fish and waves
catalogueTitle: Bowl with Fish and Waves in Relief
alt: A pale green shallow bowl is photographed from the side.
fact: The museum catalogues this celadon bowl as decorated with fish and waves in relief.
focus: Check how much the outside view lets you see of the interior.
limit: The side view gives a profile. A closer interior view is needed to check the relief described in the catalogue.

title: Landscape with Streams and Mountains
context: Attributed to Korea, late Joseon period.
material: Ink and color on paper with a silk border
alt: Mountains and streams appear on pale paper inside a blue-grey border.
fact: The museum records separate dimensions for the painting and for the object with its silk border.
focus: Find where the painted area ends and the textile border begins.
limit: The full mount view includes the border. Keep the painting size and the mounted size on separate lines.

title: Yakan seputangan
context: Made by the Yakan people of Basilan, Philippines, according to the museum.
material: plain weave with paired weft: cotton; supplementary weft: silk
alt: A square headcloth shows a checker of red and purple fields inside an outer band.
fact: The museum records paired weft in cotton plain weave with supplementary silk weft.
focus: Compare one pair of differently coloured neighbouring squares.
limit: Colours that print the same shade can still represent distinct threads in the object. Keep the materials with the collection view.

title: Binakol textile fragment
context: Attributed to Ilocos Norte, Luzon, Philippines, with an uncertain early 1900s date.
alt: Dark bands divide a textile fragment into columns of dense geometric repeats.
fact: The museum records a woven cotton fragment. The pattern creates a visual impression of movement.
focus: Follow a stable dark band while looking across the changing geometric repeats.
limit: The impression of movement belongs to a viewer and a view. The accession belongs to the stationary textile fragment.

title: Vietnamese covered jar
material: stoneware with blue and white decoration
dimensions: Diameter: 21.8 cm (8 9/16 in.); with cover: 23 cm (9 1/16 in.)
alt: A rounded jar has blue birds, clouds and other motifs on a pale ground.
fact: The museum describes a blue and white phoenix among clouds and lists a height with the cover.
focus: Check which long marks belong to the bird and which sit in the field of clouds.
limit: The picture and the measure serve different purposes. The height entry includes the cover.
